claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
claims.source_checked: Pyramid side from Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph); Cleopatra side from Roller, Cleopatra: A Biography (Oxford University Press, 2010), ISBN 978-0-19-536553-5: publisher's preview PDF (front matter, Introduction, start of ch. 1) https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9780199711000_A35484074/preview-9780199711000_A35484074.pdf; page numbers not visible in the extract; NASA, Apollo 11 mission page https://www.nasa.gov/mission/apollo-11/ (page text and image caption, via Firecrawl, cached 2026-11-17)
claims.note: What a viewer who swipes at second two takes away: Cleopatra's lifetime sits closer in time to 1969 than to the Great Pyramid's construction. That is true. PNAS 2022: 'the accession date of Khufu ranges from 2613 to 2577 BCE (1σ) according to the 14C-based chronology', 'other sources place the onset of his reign at 2589 BCE (Shaw 2000), 2554 BCE (von Beckerath 1997), or 2480 ± 5 BCE' (Spence 2000, astronomical). Even on the latest of these, Khafre's accession comes at 2448 ± 5 BCE, so Khufu's pyramid is no later than about 2450 BC. That is still about 2,384 years before 69 BC, against 2,037 years from 69 BC to 1969. Roller: 'Cleopatra VII (69–30 b.c.)'. Measured from her death (30 BC) the margin only grows. 'The building of' is safe: building started at or after Khufu's accession, which is earlier still. The popular form of this fact is true, so A4 passes. Caveat: the script's own SOURCES entry 1 cites only World History Encyclopedia and New World Encyclopedia (A2 fail). Replace them with the sources named here (see claim 13).

claims.claim: The pyramid was finished around twenty-five sixty BC.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph); Erdil et al. 2025, PLOS ONE, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314612, full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119019/ (Introduction, Table 4, Discussion)
claims.note: No source I read states a completion year. 'Around 2560' is derived from the end of Khufu's reign. PNAS 2022 attributes the pyramid to him ('the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu Pyramid)'; the Journal of Merer records limestone being taken 'to the construction site of the Great Pyramid of Khufu'). It also gives the accession dates that bracket the end of his reign: Khufu 2589 BCE and Khafre 2558 BCE on Shaw's chronology; Khufu 2613–2577 and Khafre 2586–2548 BCE (1σ) on the radiocarbon model. On either chronology the end of the reign, and so completion, falls about 2590–2550 BC. 'Around 2560' fits, and 'around' is needed. Erdil et al. 2025 (radiocarbon): 'our results act to reaffirm the High chronological estimates ... the Low chronological position ... is ruled out at 95% probability' for the Old Kingdom. So the high (c. 2560) placing is the best-supported one. Lower published dates exist (von Beckerath, Spence: 30–110 years later). A3 requires that disagreement to be recorded in SOURCES, and at present it is not (claim 13). Shaw 2000 and Bronk Ramsey 2010 were not opened directly (archive.org and science.org are blocked here); their figures are as reported in PNAS 2022, which is itself peer-reviewed.

claims.claim: To Cleopatra, the pyramids were already ancient history.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph); Diodorus Siculus 1.63.5, Loeb trans. (Oldfather), https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Diodorus_Siculus/1C*.html
claims.note: This is a framing, and it follows from the arithmetic. In context, 'the pyramids' means those at Giza. Menkaure's, the youngest, has an accession date of 2564–2524 BCE (14C) or 2532 BCE (Shaw), as given in PNAS 2022, so all three were about 2,450 or more years old at her birth. Diodorus, a Greek writing in the 1st century BC, says of the largest pyramid: 'no fewer than a thousand years have elapsed, as they say, to our lifetime, or, as some writers have it, more than three thousand four hundred'. To people of her era they were already of vast, uncertain age. I did not re-check Diodorus's own dating of his visit to Egypt. Optional: say 'the Giza pyramids' (see claim 22 on the title).

claims.claim: 2,491 YEARS (count, pyramid to Cleopatra's birth)
claims.source_checked: Arithmetic recomputed (astronomical years: 2560 BC=-2559, 69 BC=-68, 30 BC=-29); src/shorts/cleopatra-timeline/index.tsx (YEAR, SHARE) and src/shorts/cleopatra-cutout/index.tsx read; Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph)
claims.note: The arithmetic is right: -68 - (-2559) = 2491. But a four-digit exact count claims one-year precision for a span whose start is only 'c. 2560 BC'. On the radiocarbon brackets the true figure lies anywhere between about 2,480 and 2,520. The description already says 'about 2,491'. Mark it the same way on screen, e.g. '≈2,491 YEARS' or 'ABOUT 2,500 YEARS', or show the count beside the 'c.' date with a 'c.' of its own (A3/A6).

claims.claim: Old Kingdom chronology carries an uncertainty of several decades ... published dates for Khufu differ by that much between chronologies (SOURCES entry 1; description: 'Old Kingdom dates are uncertain by decades, which does not change the comparison')
claims.where: SOURCES block entry 1 and metadata: description
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph); Erdil et al. 2025, PLOS ONE, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314612, full text https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12119019/ (Introduction, Table 4, Discussion)
claims.note: This understates the spread. PNAS 2022 lists Khufu accession dates of 2613–2577 BCE (14C, 1σ), 2589 (Shaw), 2554 (von Beckerath) and 2480 ± 5 BCE (Spence), a range of over a century. Erdil et al. 2025: 'Offsets between the two [High and Low chronologies] can be as great as a century'. The second half is still true: even 2480 BC leaves the comparison intact (claim 1). Changes needed: (a) description: 'Published dates for Khufu differ by up to about a century; the latest still puts the pyramid some 2,400 years before Cleopatra.' (b) SOURCES entry 1 (A1/A2/A3): replace World History Encyclopedia and New World Encyclopedia with A2 sources (Shaw ed. 2000; Bronk Ramsey et al. 2010 Science doi:10.1126/science.1189395; Sheisha et al. 2022 PNAS doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119; Erdil et al. 2025). Record the lower chronologies (von Beckerath 2554; Spence 2480 ± 5) and why c. 2560 was chosen (radiocarbon supports the High chronology). claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramids
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, full text at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9477388/ (Introduction and chronology paragraph)
claims.note: This overstates what the script and its sources claim. The script compares her with the Great Pyramid, and the sources read support it for the three Giza pyramids (Menkaure's accession 2564–2524 BCE (14C) or 2532 BCE (Shaw); even Spence's 2415 ± 10 BCE leaves about 2,345 years to 69 BC, against 2,037). But 'the pyramids' with no qualifier includes pyramids built much later: Middle Kingdom royal pyramids, and Nubian pyramids at Meroë that were still being built in her lifetime. A pedant will point to those (A4; E2: the title must match what the short claims). I did not open an A2 source for the later pyramids; the fix rests on the title saying more than the sources checked support. Change it to '...than to the Great Pyramid' or '...than to the building of the Great Pyramid'. The on-screen 'THE PYRAMIDS?' card follows the spoken line and is fine in context.
